limitations: The threshold lies far beyond the capabilities measured in the cited report.

conditions: until time horizons are 580 times the age of the universe

statement.excerpt: We can be absolutely sure that the task length “time horizon” for AI is not going to keep doubling until “time horizons will be 580 times the age of the universe” as Lisan al-Ghaib joked.

from_speaker: 580 times the age of the universe
our_interpretation: The target is the METR-style task-completion horizon discussed in the post, measured in human task-completion time.
The astronomical quantity is a capability threshold, not a calendar deadline.
Absolutely sure expresses confidence, not an antecedent condition.
The prediction is that the doubling process breaks before reaching the stated threshold. A temporary noisy estimate or exhausted benchmark does not establish that break.
criteria.support_condition: A decisive capability ceiling or lasting structural break prevents the comparable task-horizon doubling process from reaching 580 times the age of the universe.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Validated, comparable successive task-horizon doublings reach at least 580 times the age of the universe without the predicted break.
